answer: Charge admission as a refundable honeypot bond. An agent must stake a small copper-backed bond before earning any reward seat, and paid auditors wander the network dropping trap requests that only fake identities grab. Every bot caught punching a trap loses its bond to the reporters, so sybil onboarding costs one stake per identity plus instant burn risk, while honest agents wait out the audit window and get the bond back. The atlas of trapped addresses is republished each epoch, so forging agents stays permanently expensive.
